svg.title: redisq: how another consumer finds out that a consumer died holding jobs without calling Close
svg.desc: Two rows show the same start on one clock, in real seconds (times not to scale). Consumer C2 holds two jobs, J1 and J2, that it dequeued and has not acknowledged: they sit in the pending hash under its owner ID. Its own sweep, once a second, has just renewed its heartbeat to now plus 30 seconds and its presence mark is 0, meaning a sweep has seen it subscribed to its wake channel. Consumer C1 is alive, idle, and sweeps once a second. At 0.1 s C2 stops without calling Close, so it sweeps no more. A sweep moves the shared clock only if half a second has passed since the last move, and only a sweep that moves it checks subscribers: C1's sweep at 0.3 s comes 0.3 s after C2's last sweep moved the clock, so it checks heartbeats but not subscribers. Row A, process killed: Redis drops the dead process's subscription at once. C1's sweep at 1.3 s moves the clock, finds no subscriber and sets C2's presence mark to 1.3. At 6.3 s a sweep finds C2 gone for 5 seconds and takes it for dead: J1 and J2 go back to the front of the list in one step (J2 at the head), and C2's heartbeat and mark are dropped although the heartbeat had time left. Row B, host lost: Redis keeps the lost host's socket open, so it still counts C2's subscription and the mark stays 0. C2's heartbeat runs out at 30 s and C1's sweep at 30.3 s takes C2 for dead, with the same requeue. In both rows the requeue wakes C1, which pops J2 and then J1, runs them and acknowledges them, leaving the list and the pending hash empty. Row A got its jobs back after about 6.3 seconds, row B after about 30.3. The picture then fades back to the start.

g.text: time left before C2 counts as dead
C2 counts as dead at 30 s
gone 5 s: C2 counts as dead
C2's own sweep at 0 s: renews its heartbeat, moves the shared clock
C1's sweep at 0.3 s: clock moved 0.3 s ago (< .5 s), so no presence check
C1's sweep at 1.3 s moves the clock: no subscriber, so mark = 1.3
C1's sweep at 6.3 s: gone 5 s, so C2 is dead: J1, J2 to the list front
wake → C1 pops J2, then J1
J1, J2 back in the list at 6.3 s
B · host lost (Redis keeps its socket)
C2 counts as dead at 30 s
C2's own sweep at 0 s: renews its heartbeat, moves the shared clock
C1's sweep at 0.3 s: clock moved 0.3 s ago (< .5 s), so no presence check
C1's sweep at 1.3 s: C2's subscriber still counted, so mark stays 0
C1's sweep at 30.3 s: heartbeat ran out, so C2 is dead: J1, J2 to the list front
wake → C1 pops J2, then J1
J1, J2 back in the list at 30.3 s
